generationMethod: Independent audit of the actual MC-17 working tree: repository inspection, independent WCAG recomputation, independent registry audit, re-execution of validator/unit/typecheck/build/Playwright gates, and a mutation harness around the real validator. scope: MC-17/36 internal design system only: src/app/marea-design-system/**, preview/**, e2e/design-system/**, docs/marea/design-system/**, the named scripts and the isolated catalogue build. knownLimitations: Historical limitations recorded by the first two reviews are retained in sections 9-10 of MC17-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW.md and in this dataset; they are not current-state claims.
Visual baselines are Chromium/Windows-specific; two 320x812 instrument captures were refreshed for renderer drift after a before/after review. A later environment change needs a new platform suffix.
Axe 0 violations / 36 passes / 0 incomplete in four modes is automated evidence only; no screen-reader, cross-browser, real-device, glare/night-vision or WCAG 2.2 AA conformance claim exists.
Performance evidence is one laboratory run; no field/RUM data and no marine-hardware validation exists.
Hydration is argued from deterministic ids and static copy; the design system is not rendered by the public SSR server.
The 49-entry registry is an internal contract, not a public API.
Only hand-authored source is covered by Prettier; machine-generated *.generated.ts files are validated by their deterministic generators instead, as asserted by a unit test.

findings.title: Family-specific limits are declared in copy and in FAMILY_LIMIT_KEYS but are not presented; the family card drops the fifth restriction (safety/licensing/compatibility) and no rendered surface states AIS receive-only, WATCH no-guarantee, FLEET no-default-hardware, SENSE kit-once or DISPLAY no-dimensions.
findings.evidence: FAMILY_LIMIT_KEYS is defined at src/app/marea-design-system/data/commerce-presentation.adapter.ts:96-105 and is referenced by no component: `grep -r FAMILY_LIMIT_KEYS src preview e2e` returns only the definition. MareaFamilyCard builds at most four restriction labels (src/app/marea-design-system/components/commerce/marea-family-card.ts:95-104, `if (labels.length === 4) break;`) from `restrictionCopyKey()` only; it never reads FAMILY_LIMIT_KEYS. Fixture restrictions put the family-specific kind fifth for PILOT/AIS/NAV/WEATHER/FLEET/SENSE/WATCH, so the safety/licensing/compatibility chip is the one dropped. Runtime probe `.tmp/audit/rendered-copy.mjs` on the built catalogue at 127.0.0.1:4301 rendered 100 of 138 copy keys but false for aisReceiveOnly, watchNoGuarantee, fleetNoHardware, senseEssentialsKit, displayConditional and navWeatherLicensing. Runtime `marea-family-card` restriction lists for NAV, PILOT and FLEET contain only the four generic restrictions (publication, trademark, price, stock); the PILOT safety gate is visible only in a separately hand-composed marea-permission-notice elsewhere in the gallery. The catalogue renders bundle components only for START and FLEET (preview/catalogue/app/galleries/commerce.gallery.ts:167-180); the PROTECT bundle that contains SENSE-ESSENTIALS is not rendered. Docs D10 (MC17-PRODUCT-EDITION-BUNDLE-PRESENTATION.md:91-98) and D15 (MC17-BILINGUAL-PRESENTATION-CONTRACT.md:108-112) explicitly claim these limits are rendered via MareaFamilyCard and FAMILY_LIMIT_KEYS; that claim is false. Validator MC17-20 (scripts/check-marea-design-system.mjs:527-546) and MC17-23 (:590-609) only search fixture/copy strings, so both PASS while the presentation is absent.
findings.reproduction: Build and serve the catalogue (node scripts/marea-ds-preview-server.mjs after npx ng build marea-design-system-catalogue), then run node .tmp/audit/rendered-copy.mjs and inspect the familyLimitKeys object: aisReceiveOnly, watchNoGuarantee, fleetNoHardware, senseEssentialsKit, displayConditional and navWeatherLicensing are false. Inspect `document.querySelectorAll('marea-family-card .restriction')`: NAV/PILOT/FLEET each show four generic chips and no safety/licensing chip. `grep -rn FAMILY_LIMIT_KEYS src preview e2e` shows no consumer.
findings.requiredCorrection: Bind the family-specific limit copy to a rendered surface: use FAMILY_LIMIT_KEYS[familyId] in MareaFamilyCard (and/or a dedicated limit/notice component) before the generic restriction chips, or raise/reorder the cap so a safety/licensing/compatibility restriction is never dropped; render the PROTECT bundle or otherwise demonstrate SENSE-ESSENTIALS expansion; add per-family end-to-end assertions that the required sentence is visible in the catalogue. Update D10/D15 to match the implementation.
findings.correctionOwner: MC-17 design-system implementer and documentation owner, coordinated by the Lead
findings.independentReverification: At f2c9ec2 the catalogue renders nine family cards (NAV, PILOT, FLEET, AIS, WATCH, SENSE, DISPLAY, WEATHER, HUB) with stable data-testid values. Independent DOM probe (family-probe.mjs, ES and EN) confirmed each family limit inside its own card, no missing family, a material restriction first for every card with one, and the six adversarial specimens (safety first, safety fifth, duplicates, missing array, unknown kind, dual blocking). findings.title: Validator MC17-15 detects the presence of ':focus-visible' but not a hidden focus outline; a component whose focus rule is `outline: none` still passes the static check.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-marea-design-system.mjs:420-438 only tests `source.includes(':focus-visible')`. Adversarial mutation .tmp/audit/run-adversarial.mjs replaced marea-link's focus rule with `:host(:focus-visible) { outline: none; }`; the harness observed MC17-15 = PASS (recorded in .tmp/audit/adversarial-report-2.json, failureMode d-hidden-focus-outline, detected false). The Playwright accessibility test only checks the first Tab-reached button and link in web-light and instrument-night (e2e/design-system/accessibility.spec.ts:117-131), so a broader or mode-specific hidden focus ring could ship without a failing gate.
findings.reproduction: Run node .tmp/audit/make-harness.mjs then node .tmp/audit/run-adversarial.mjs; scenario d-hidden-focus-outline shows targetCheck MC17-15 observed PASS and detected false.
findings.requiredCorrection: Extend MC17-15 (or a companion static check) to reject `outline: none|0` in focus rules without an alternative visible indicator, and add a computed-style Playwright assertion for every keyboard-operable component in all four modes.
findings.independentReverification: Reproduced the original mutation: replace marea-link focus rule with ":host(:focus-visible) { outline: none; }" and run the I/O-overlay harness (.tmp/audit/make-harness.mjs + run-adversarial.mjs). MC17-15 now observes FAIL and the scenario is detected (was undetected at 3a8d4fd). The added condition is /:focus-visible[\s\S]{0,400}--marea-focus-ring/ at scripts/check-marea-design-system.mjs:433. Residual limitation: the check is textual, and there is still no computed-style Playwright assertion for every keyboard-operable component in all four modes (accessibility.spec.ts checks the first button/link in web-light and instrument-night).

findings.title: Validator MC17-13 does not actually prove the 'no undocumented variant' claim: it scans only inline literal unions in the input type argument, ignores aliased enums/default values, and its detail string has a dead arithmetic expression.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-marea-design-system.mjs:365-391. The extraction regex `input<([^>]*)>` captures the type text and then only single-quoted literals inside it; aliased enums such as MareaTextVariant and defaults such as `input<MareaButtonVariant>('action')` contribute nothing. The detail at :388 is `${documented} option values and ${registry.components.length * 0 || ''} variants documented`, which always prints an empty count. The independent registry audit (tmp/audit/registry-audit2.mjs) found visualVariants inconsistently aggregates behavioural enums: marea-notice includes off/polite/assertive (live input), marea-accordion includes single/multiple (mode input), marea-permission-notice includes live values but not its `kind` values. The actual visual variants are documented in the registry, so this is an evidence-quality defect, not a missing feature.
findings.reproduction: Read the check; run node .tmp/audit/registry-audit2.mjs and observe the mismatches for marea-notice/accordion/permission-notice; run the validator and inspect the MC17-13 detail line '39 option values and  variants documented'.
findings.requiredCorrection: Resolve named type aliases and default values, compare each option-like input's full value set with the registry, fix the detail string, and normalise visualVariants so it consistently means 'visual option values' (including live/mode/kind where those are part of the documented API).
findings.independentReverification: At f2c9ec2 MC17-13 is a TypeScript-compiler-based comparison: 33 option inputs resolved to 126 string values, compared in both directions with the registry (documented type text and visualVariants); 64 visual variants matched and 4 broad non-enumerable inputs are reported as skipped, not silently ignored. The mutation harness detected an aliased union with an undocumented value and an enum-valued input with an undocumented value (2/2). The dead arithmetic detail was removed.

findings.title: The working tree changed during the audit: a concurrent workstream renamed marea-commerce-cta to marea-commercial-cta and added a testIgnore to the public Playwright config at 03:31:53; the audit re-ran all gates after the change.
findings.evidence: At the start of the audit, git status showed marea-commerce-cta.ts modified; at 03:31:53 it had been deleted and marea-commercial-cta.ts added, with component-registry.json, component-states.json, preview galleries, e2e/commerce.spec.ts, docs and playwright.config.ts (`testIgnore: ['**/design-system/**']`) rewritten. All reported gates were re-run after the tree stabilized (validator 36/38, unit 27/27, tsc 0, build 0, Playwright 28/28). This is a reproducibility/process finding, not a code defect: the final reviewed state is the post-rename tree.
findings.reproduction: Inspect file mtimes around 03:31:53 and `git status --porcelain`; `git diff playwright.config.ts` shows the testIgnore addition. Re-run the full gate on a frozen SHA to avoid a moving target.
findings.requiredCorrection: Freeze the working tree before the final independent gate; include the rename and the testIgnore change in the reviewed commit; do not edit during a review.
findings.independentReverification: The reviewed state is one frozen commit (7cbc99e); git status --porcelain was empty before and after every gate and git diff HEAD --quiet exits 0. The only tracked file written by the suite (evidence/axe-summary.json, generatedAt) was byte-restored; no file changed during the re-review.

findings.title: The MC17-15 focus heuristic still accepted a transparent outline colour and a zero-width/transparent focus treatment that references the focus token
findings.evidence: At 4a9043b focusContractProblems did not exist; the validator only matched /:focus-visible[\s\S]{0,400}--marea-focus-ring/. An I/O-overlay mutation adding `outline-color: transparent` after the token-based outline passed MC17-15, and the earlier `outline: none` form was detected only by the string heuristic added in the first correction.
findings.reproduction: Mutate marea-link.ts focus rule to keep `outline: var(--marea-focus-width) var(--marea-focus-style) var(--marea-focus-ring)` and add `outline-color: transparent;`; run the validator: MC17-15 observed PASS at 4a9043b. The same mutation is rejected at f2c9ec2.
findings.requiredCorrection: Reject outline: none/0, outline-style: none, zero outline-width and transparent outline colours inside every :focus-visible rule, while still requiring the focus-ring token; add tests.
findings.correctionOwner: design-system validator owner (implementation agent), reviewed by the independent auditor
findings.independentReverification: At f2c9ec2 focusContractProblems rejects transparent outline/outline-color, outline none/0 and zero-width styles. Independent mutation harness: hidden focus and transparent focus mutations are both detected (2/2), and the design-system unit suite includes a real-component transparent-mutation test (41/41 pass).
